question.text: Suppose \(f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) be given by \(f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}1, \quad \text { if } x=1 \\ e^{\left(x^{10}-1\right)}+(x-1)^2 \sin \frac{1}{x-1}\end{array}\right., \text { if } x \neq 1 \text { then }\)

solution.text:
Hint: \(f: R \rightarrow R f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc} 1 & \text { if } x=1 & \\  e^{\left(x^{10}-1\right)} &+(x-1)^2  &\cdot \sin \left(\frac{1}{x-1}\right) \text { if } x \neq 1\end{array}\right.\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& f\left(1^{-}\right)=1+0=1 \\
& f\left(1^{+}\right)=1+0=1 \\
& f(1)=1 \\
& \therefore \quad f(x) \text { is continuous at } x=1 \\
& f^{\prime}(x)=\left\{e^{\left(x^{10}-1\right)} \cdot\left(10 x^5\right)+2(x-1) \cdot \sin \left(\frac{1}{x-1}\right)-(x-1)^2 \cdot \cos \left(\frac{1}{x-1}\right) \cdot\left(\frac{1}{x-1}\right)^2\right\}
\end{aligned}\)
which does not exist.
